market.headline: Tech gave back part of Monday's relief rally: QQQ fell 2.0% and SPY 0.5%, led by AI chips as Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia became a political and national-security story. The regime is still RED and hostile, so protect cash until Wednesday's 08:30 PCE report.
market.day_type: AI-chip selloff and rotation: Monday's 7.0% QQQ bounce faded as the Nvidia news turned negative, so traders sold the chip stocks with the most risk (MU, CRWV, AMD, ARM, SMCI) and moved into Apple, Microsoft and Netflix, which all closed up.
watch: Wed 08:30: GDP and October PCE inflation. The Fed's Williams just pointed to higher rates over time, so a hot print hits the expensive tech names hardest.
QQQ 631.15 (today's low): a break opens the way to the 20-day low of 606.23. A close back above 641.95 means the selloff is over for now.
SPY 712.14 (today's low): holding it keeps the drop orderly. SPY now sits below its 200-day average of 730.62, which puts that level overhead as resistance.

stocks.headline: Fell 5.9% to 155.38, then slipped to 153.82 after hours, as Huang's return drew political fire. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: The business did not change today. Sales grew 106% and profit per share kept pace, margins are improving and next year's forecast rose 28% in 90 days. At 21× trailing profit, the lowest in 5 years, the stock is cheap. The damage is political. Republicans and an op-ed say the president forcing Huang back is a national-security risk, the FBI and the Attorney General would not discuss an investigation, and Huang told staff Nvidia needs no succession plan. That keeps a lid on the stock and pulls down its suppliers (MU, TSM, ARM, SMCI) and buyers like CRWV.

long_term.reason: The earnings power is strong and the price is cheap. Still, the CEO and governance story is getting worse, and an investigation or new limits on China sales would hit the stock directly, so don't add yet.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the investigation story fades and the stock closes back above 159.92, it moves to Add on dips. Any formal probe or new China restriction moves it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy tomorrow's open or ahead of PCE. Add only if it closes back above 159.92. If it breaks 150.50, stay out.

levels.means: above = the Huang selloff is being bought and adding is OK; below = sellers stay in control
above = today's low holds; below = the drop is extending and adding should wait
above = the 52-week low is intact; below = the long-term trend is broken

stocks.headline: Fell 11.0% to 629.79, the worst large-chip drop of the day, with no company news. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: This was a high-beta stock dumped with the Nvidia story. Nothing changed at the company. Sales grew 345%, operating margin is 75%, the backlog is 134.0B, debt is only 2.8B against 38.4B of cash, and it trades at 3× next year's forecast. The risk is the cycle: memory profits this high attract supply, and the market is already pricing a peak. The Dec 17 report decides it. Until then it moves about twice as much as QQQ in both directions.

long_term.reason: The numbers are exceptional and the price is low, but memory is a boom-and-bust business. Hold what you own and let the Dec 17 report confirm before adding.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A Dec 17 report that shows demand still speeding up moves it to Buy. A break below 585.25 before then means the market is calling the peak, and it moves to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the dip tomorrow. Add only if it closes back above 666.66. If it closes below 585.25, take no new shares until Dec 17.

levels.means: above = today's drop is fully repaired and adding is OK; below = the selloff still has control
above = today's low holds; below = it is heading back toward the 20-day low
above = the November floor holds; below = the market is pricing a memory peak

stocks.headline: Fell 8.9% to 413.27, down 17.9% in five days, and lost its 200-day average of 432.0. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: AMD is the main alternative to Nvidia, so it was sold as part of the same chip trade. It is also volatile, moving about twice as much as QQQ. The business is strong: sales grew 45% and are speeding up, operating margin doubled to 18%, and 35 analysts raised forecasts while 3 cut. But it trades at 98× trailing profit, above peers, so it falls harder when chips sell off. Falling under the 200-day average turns the chart from a pullback into a downtrend.

long_term.reason: Growth is real, but the price still assumes it continues and the chart just broke. A better entry will come once it is back above the 200-day average.

stocks.what_would_change_it: Two closes back above 432.0 move it to Add on dips. A close below 396.03 means the decline has further to run.
stocks.action: Don't buy tomorrow. Buy a first piece only after a full session closes above 432.0.
